text.title: Context File Failure Modes
text.summary: Six ways a project context file turns into a standing tax, each with the observable symptom and the rule that prevents it.

failure.symptom: Every module has an `AGENTS.md`, all written in the same voice, all containing a directory tree. Nobody can name the last time one was edited by hand.
failure.cause: A bootstrap pass generated them and the workflow advanced without a human cut, so the repository shipped the exact variant that measured negative.
failure.prevention: Machine output is a draft. The phase that created it does not advance until a human has cut it, and a repo-wide generation pass is forbidden.

failure.symptom: The context file is 600 lines. Every individual addition was reasonable at the time and nobody has ever removed one.
failure.cause: No ceiling was declared, so growth had no opposing force; the cost of each line is charged to a future session whose occupant is not in the room to object.
failure.prevention: Declare the ceiling, resolve overflow by relocation or cutting, and never raise the ceiling silently.

failure.symptom: A third of the file is a directory tree and a dependency table. The agent could have listed either in one tool call, and frequently does anyway.
failure.cause: Background was mistaken for instruction, so a derivable fact became a per-turn charge — and, worse, a constraint the agent honours instead of looking.
failure.prevention: Classify every line; overviews are cut or relocated and may never be kept. Commands, conventions and boundaries are what remains.

failure.symptom: The agent refuses a reasonable approach, or contorts a task, citing a line that was only ever a note about what the team usually does.
failure.cause: Over-compliance. An unmarked soft line reads as a hard constraint, and the agent has no way to tell a habit from a rule.
failure.prevention: Say "prefer" or "unless the task says otherwise" in the line itself, or cut it. Unmarked guidance is judged as an instruction.

failure.symptom: A monorepo with eight nested context files. Sessions are noticeably more expensive than the same work in a single-package repo and nobody has isolated why.
failure.cause: Subtree-specific content lives in always-loaded files, so every session pays for rules governing directories it never touches.
failure.prevention: Relocate subtree content to a path-scoped mechanism and name the destination in the record. Coverage is unchanged; the charge becomes conditional.

failure.symptom: "The context file clearly helps" — based on one run each way, with the cost side never mentioned.
failure.cause: The effect sizes at stake are a few percentage points against run-to-run variance that exceeds them, so a single pair confirms whatever the author already believed.
failure.prevention: Five runs per arm minimum, medians, and the cost delta in currency reported next to the success delta. A cost rise with no measured success rise resolves to cut or delete.
